work_order.understanding: PR #91 shipped a release-notes gate whose walk is recursive, while the publisher that turns notes into a changelog (parseReleaseNotes in packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs) is still a single non-recursive fs.readdir at line 160. The two disagree about the same directory and the disagreement is invisible to every check in the repo: release-notes-check.mjs selects nested notes through a recursive git diff pathspec, count-points.mjs counts them under 'upcoming-release-notes/**/*', release-notes-generate.mjs lists them with 'git ls-tree -r', and the docs generator shares parseReleaseNotes. Only the publisher drops them. A note in a subdirectory is validated by the gate (exit 0), counted for points, listed for unlinking, and then silently omitted from the changelog and the docs page, credited to nobody. The gate's own doc comment (release-notes-gate.mjs:22-35) already asserts nested notes are published, so the code claims the opposite of what it does, and that comment is what has to be rewritten by this change. Six smaller findings travel with it: the test suite writes its hostile fixture into the real shared notes directory with only a finally to clean it up and no gitignore entry, so a killed vitest poisons every later run; both gate scripts throw a raw ENOENT stack trace when the notes directory is missing; the gate exports three defaulted dir parameters and a validateNote no caller passes or imports; and its sort comparator is a three-line copy of Array.prototype.sort's default under a comment that misattributes the property to avoiding a locale-sensitive comparison. Two of the ten reported items are not code changes: the stale 'Validated 92' count lived in PR #91's work-order.json (a file this repo does not keep), and the understated PR body is GitHub metadata on a merged PR. Both are answered here rather than implemented. This is version 2: it answers the three objections to version 1 directly — AC-4 and AC-5 now have tests[] cases behind them instead of conceding 'the suite cannot cover this', AC-6's how_to_verify no longer greps for a string this repository does not produce, and AC-2 no longer claims a set equality that the `only` filter refutes.
work_order.root_cause: Two independent enumerations of one directory, one rule each. The gate's walk (release-notes-gate.mjs:36-56) recurses; the publisher's (util.mjs:160) does not. Every other participant — the git diff pathspec, the count-points glob, the ls-tree -r at release-notes-generate.mjs:139 — is recursive, so the non-recursive readdir is the single outlier, and the gate added in #91 widened the split rather than closing it.
work_order.approach:
One walk, one rule, in the module both sides already import. Move the recursive walk out of the gate and into packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs as an exported listNotePaths(dir) returning every note path relative to the directory, forward-slashed and sorted by the default Array.prototype.sort (which compares UTF-16 code units, is deterministic, and is not the locale-sensitive localeCompare the old comment claimed to avoid). parseReleaseNotes uses that walk, so the publisher selects exactly what the gate selects. The gate imports the walk and keeps its exported listNotePaths as a one-line wrapper supplying its NOTES_DIR default, so the gate's public surface is unchanged and there is exactly one implementation of the rule.

The shared walk is SYNCHRONOUS, which is a deliberate change from version 1. util.mjs gains one import (`import * as fsSync from 'node:fs'`) rather than becoming an async walk, and that keeps listNotePaths, collectFailures and main synchronous in the gate exactly as they are today. Version 1 made them async and told the implementer to await four call sites in release-notes-check.test.mjs; a missed await there turns `expect(collectFailures()).toEqual([])` into an assertion on a Promise that passes vacuously, which version 1 named as its own top risk. Synchronous removes that risk by making it unrepresentable, and it is also the smaller diff: the gate is a CLI whose every other operation is already `node:fs` sync. parseReleaseNotes is already async and calls the synchronous walk without awaiting, which costs nothing. util.mjs already exports a mix of synchronous functions (selectReleaseNotePaths, formatNotes, describeAuthor), so this is not a new shape for the module.

Rewrite the doc comment above the gate's listNotePaths (lines 22-35) rather than deleting it. It currently states that the two enumerations 'already disagree about the same directory, because one is fed a recursive git diff pathspec and the other a single readdir' — after this change that sentence is false, and leaving it would have the file asserting the defect it no longer has. The replacement names the shared rule and the participants that must agree with it.

The `only` filter keeps working by matching on the relative path: release-notes-generate.mjs:143-144 already builds its allow-list from 'git ls-tree -r' with the prefix stripped, so a nested note already arrives as 'sub/deep.md'; the filter was written against flat basenames and now compares the same relative string it is handed. A top-level basename therefore no longer matches a nested note, which is correct. With no `only` argument the filter is the identity, so parseReleaseNotes' `files` equals listNotePaths(dir) exactly — that equality is what AC-2 asserts, and it is asserted only for the no-`only` case. The `only`-filtered behaviour is its own clause (AC-8), never folded into the equality claim.

resolvePrNumber needs no change: it calls join(dir, name) for both the read and the git log pathspec, which resolves 'sub/deep.md' correctly, and its numeric shortcut now falls through to git log and returns the same number it would have. Do not 'fix' that. The README rule is the gate's rule exactly — exclude README.md only at the top level, matching selectReleaseNotePaths and the existing gate walk; a nested README.md being validated as a note is the correct outcome of that shared rule, not a bug to route around.

Findings 2 and 6 pull in opposite directions — 2 asks for a temporary directory collectFailures accepts as an override, 6 asks for the dir parameter to be deleted because no caller passes it. Both are satisfied by the same edit: the fixture moves to os.tmpdir() and passes its path, giving the parameter a real caller, while validateNote keeps dir (collectFailures passes it; it is the one function that needs it to join the relative path) and loses its export since nothing imports it. That is the reviewer's own stated alternative, so no gitignore entry and no beforeAll/afterAll assertion is needed — the fixture is outside the repository, so a killed vitest cannot poison a later run. listNotePaths gains the same real caller from the new util.test.js cases.

The ENOENT guard goes in collectFailures rather than main(), where the reviewer put it. Same output — a failure string main() already prints as '::error::' before process.exit(1) — but reachable by the unit suite, which cannot reach main() (not exported, imported by nothing, and NOTES_DIR is resolved from import.meta.url so a subprocess cannot be pointed elsewhere without deleting the real directory). The message names the directory it was handed, 'cannot read <dir>: <error.message>', rather than a fixed string, because a fixed one would misreport the tmpdir the test passes.

The same guard goes into release-notes-check.mjs:20, which QA measured producing an identical stack trace on an unchanged file. That is pre-existing behaviour rather than a regression and the reviewer named only the gate, but the two scripts sit in the same package and ship the same defect. reportError is a hoisted function declaration, so the top-level call site can use it, and it exits 1 on both paths, so the exit code is unchanged. Unlike the reviewer's claim, this one IS reachable by the suite: runCheck (release-notes-check.test.mjs:76-91) already drives SCRIPT_PATH as a subprocess with cwd=dir, and createRepo's notes directory can simply be removed before the run — so AC-4 gets a real tests[] case rather than the manual procedure version 1 deferred.

main() loses its export; with the ENOENT guard in collectFailures, both behaviours worth covering are covered. Acceptance criteria assert exit codes and message shapes, never a literal note count — the direct lesson from AC-5 of PR #91, where 'Validated 92' on a branch yielding 93 nearly failed a passing change.

work_order.debate_summary: plan/brief.md records no decisions for this issue, so nothing was overridden and no prior answer constrained this order. The brief does carry the rejection of version 1, and this version answers all three of its objections rather than restating the plan. Objection 1 held that AC-4 and AC-5 were verify:"test" criteria with no tests[] case behind them, and that the 'cannot be covered' claim was false because runCheck(dir) already drives the script as a subprocess and createRepo's only mkdir is the directory in question. That is correct and the plan was wrong to defer it — the missing-directory path for release-notes-check.mjs is reachable by removing one directory after setup(). Version 2 adds that case (asserting only the stable '::error::Cannot read upcoming-release-notes/: ' prefix, never the platform-varying ENOENT text), adds a second case asserting the suite's fixture never lands in the repository so AC-5 has a case of its own, rewrites both how_to_verify steps to name their cases, and deletes the out_of_scope entry that deferred the subprocess case and the risks bullet that told QA the suite could not cover AC-4 — both of which would have been false. Objection 2 held that AC-6's grep was false against this repository: `grep -rn release-notes-gate packages/` returns four lines across two files, including the lage wiring this plan explicitly leaves alone and the assertion AC-6 itself relies on. I ran both forms; the import form returns exactly one line, so AC-6's how_to_verify now uses it and says why the bare string is the wrong probe. The same objection caught an inaccuracy in AC-6's check clause — the suite does not pass a temporary directory to both functions, because the pre-existing calls at :236 and :240 are argument-less on purpose and the non-empty-set guard depends on them — so the clause now says what is true: no dir parameter exists that no caller supplies. Objection 3 held that AC-2's headline claim, 'for any directory the set listNotePaths returns equals the set parseReleaseNotes enumerates', is refuted by the ticket's own filter cases, since with an `only` filter parseReleaseNotes returns a strict subset. That is right and it is the most dangerous kind of error in a work order, because AC-2 is the sentence stating the whole thesis. AC-2 is now scoped to the no-`only` case and names the comparison it rests on, a new tests[] case asserts files deep-equals listNotePaths(dir) over a tmpdir fixture holding top.md, sub/deep.md and sub/README.md — which the previous version could not, because both of its cases exercised listNotePaths alone and never called parseReleaseNotes — and the filter behaviour moves to its own criterion, AC-8. Beyond answering the objections, version 2 makes one substantive change of its own: the shared walk is synchronous rather than async, which removes the missed-await hazard version 1 named as its own top risk and shrinks the diff by four call sites. That trade is stated in files[] and risks[] rather than left implicit. The rest of version 1's reasoning stands: findings 2 and 6 are satisfied by the same edit (move the fixture to os.tmpdir() and pass its path, giving the dir parameter a real caller, so no gitignore entry and no stale-leftover assertion is needed); the ENOENT guard sits in collectFailures rather than main() because main() is unreachable from a test while the output is byte-identical either way; the message names the directory it was handed rather than a fixed string, because a fixed one would misreport the tmpdir the test passes; and release-notes-check.mjs is included because QA measured it throwing an identical stack trace on a file PR #91 never touched, which is now both cheap to fix and cheap to test — though it is flagged in risks as the one file a maintainer may reasonably want dropped.
residual_risks: The rule is now in one function, but nothing enforces that a future fourth participant recurses. A release-notes publisher added outside packages/ci-actions would reintroduce exactly this defect, and the gate would again validate a note that no reader sees.

The gate's doc comment at lines 22-35 is the thing that caused this bug to be believed fixed, because it described a divergence the code did not repair. Rewriting it is part of the change rather than a follow-up, but the general hazard remains: a comment that asserts a property no test holds is how the next reader is misled.

collectFailures now returns a synthetic failure string on a read error rather than throwing. A caller that distinguished 'the notes are valid' from 'the notes could not be read' by catching an exception would now see a failure list instead — correct for main(), but it changes the function's contract for any future caller.

The two QA-reported behaviours and six review-reported behaviours are fixed together in one branch. A regression anywhere in that branch is harder to attribute than six independent changes would be; the split was rejected because the findings share a cause, and that trade is being made deliberately.

review.title: The ENOENT guard in release-notes-check.mjs does not stop the script in the shape CI runs it. reportError only calls process.exit(1) synchronously when GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is unset; when it is set — always true on a GitHub Actions runner — it opens a write stream and returns, deferring the exit to the stream's close event. Execution falls through the new try/catch into the BASE_REF handling and the async git IIFE. A missing notes directory still runs a network `git fetch` and `git diff`, then prints a SECOND, misleading ::error:: line claiming no release note was added — the opposite diagnosis from the one the guard just reported.

A missing notes directory still runs a network `git fetch` and `git diff`, then prints a SECOND, misleading ::error:: line claiming no release note was added — the opposite diagnosis from the one the guard just reported.

`packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs:20`

Evidence: Ran the PR's script against a throwaway repo with upcoming-release-notes/ removed, CI shape (GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY set, BASE_REF set), with a PATH shim logging git invocations:
::error::Cannot read upcoming-release-notes/: ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '.../upcoming-release-notes'
::notice::
::error::No release note added or modified under upcoming-release-notes/. Add a *.md file describing your change, or edit an existing note.
::notice::
--- git invoked after the guard ---
GIT fetch origin base
GIT diff --name-status -z --diff-filter=AMR origin/base...HEAD -- upcoming-release-notes/
With a normally-fast summary file the stream closes before `git fetch` returns and only one error line appears (5/5 runs), but `git fetch` is still spawned every time — verified against a valid origin, which logged `GIT fetch origin base`. With an unreachable origin and a blocked summary the script dies with an unhandled-rejection stack trace (exit 124 under timeout), the exact output AC-4 says is fixed. The new test cannot catch this: runCheck (release-notes-check.test.mjs:76-81) does `delete env.GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` before spawning, so AC-4's only coverage runs the branch where the guard works.

Fix: Make the guard terminate rather than rely on reportError's deferred exit: move the `Looking in` probe into the async IIFE and `return` from it on failure (the shape the rest of the file already uses), or set a module-level flag and process.exit(1) after the reportError call. Add a test case that runs runCheck with GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY pointed at a real file so the CI shape is covered.

Evidence: A notes dir with a top-level note and an unreadable subdirectory:
$ chmod 000 /tmp/eacces/notes/locked
$ collectFailures('/tmp/eacces/notes')
[ 'cannot read /tmp/eacces/notes: EACCES: permission denied, scandir \'/tmp/eacces/notes/locked\'' ]

validated_work_order.understanding:
Two separate things went wrong. FIRST, the plan reviewer is right and this revision corrects his objection: the previous work order asserted its new BUG-3 unit case 'fails today for exactly the reason QA reported', and it does not. It prescribed `runCheck(repo.dir, { GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY: <temp file> })`, but runCheck unconditionally injects `BASE_REF: BASE_BRANCH` into the child env, so that call leaves BASE_REF SET — and with BASE_REF set the unfixed script prints exactly one ::error:: line, no 'BASE_REF env var is not set' line, and exits 1, which is precisely what all three of the case's assertions require. I reproduced this directly: with the previous order's exact call, the case passes 84/84 against the UNFIXED script. The same plan contradicted itself — tests[] said 'BASE_REF unset' while files[] prescribed a call that leaves it set, and that contradiction is what produced the vacuous test. I fixed the harness as the reviewer prescribed (an env-override parameter that can DELETE a variable, merged after the BASE_REF injection, dropping undefined-valued keys rather than stringifying them — I verified Node's execFile omits undefined-valued env keys entirely) and re-ran it: with `BASE_REF: undefined` the case fails against d4684c80 and passes with the fix. AC-11's end-to-end command was already correct; the defect was confined to the unit case, as the reviewer said, and files[] now matches tests[].

SECOND, and this is the diagnosis the previous attempt got wrong. It said its root cause was RIGHT because QA confirmed the headline fix real (all eight original criteria pass; a nested note now reaches the changelog and the generated docs page). That much is true. But the previous attempt carried a premise it never examined: it treated 'the two sides must agree on WHICH files exist' as the whole invariant, and asserted a nested README.md being validated as a note is 'the correct outcome of that shared rule, not a bug to route around'. Unifying the enumeration was necessary but not sufficient. The gate and the publisher now agree on the file SET and disagree on what happens when a member of that set is malformed. The gate (validateNote) turns every malformation into a named failure string and keeps going; the publisher (parseReleaseNotes) dereferences data.authors unguarded and dies. That asymmetry was harmless while the publisher only read top-level files the gate had already cleared — an invariant the recursive walk breaks, because gate and publisher now agree a NESTED file is a note and the publisher has no validateNote equivalent. So the root cause is a behaviour-parity gap, not an enumeration gap. I reproduced all three bugs against d4684c80 myself in a worktree at that commit: BUG-1 parseReleaseNotes throws 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading map)' on any note with no authors list; BUG-2 collectFailures wraps the ENTIRE recursive walk in one try/catch, so one chmod-000 subdirectory discards every failure already accumulated; BUG-3 the new guard in release-notes-check.mjs calls reportError from module scope, but reportError only exits synchronously when GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is ABSENT — the one environment a real Actions runner never has and the one the unit harness deletes. All 83 existing tests pass on that commit; nothing here is a red suite, all three bugs sit outside coverage.

One further finding the previous attempt did not have: its BUG-2 fix text said '`path` is already imported at the top of the file', but following that literally (`join(dir, relative)`) crashes with 'ReferenceError: join is not defined' — I hit exactly that while prototyping, because release-notes-gate.mjs imports `* as path from 'node:path'` and has no bare `join` binding. The change text below names `path.join` explicitly.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The shared walk made the gate and the publisher agree on WHICH files are release notes, but nothing made them agree on WHAT a malformed member of that set does. release-notes-gate.mjs's validateNote turns every rule violation into a named failure string and keeps going; parseReleaseNotes has no equivalent and dereferences data.authors.map with no Array.isArray guard. Before this PR that was latent, because the publisher only ever read top-level files the gate had already cleared. The recursive walk routed nested files into it, so the pre-existing unguarded dereference became reachable. Two smaller instances of the same 'report, do not abort and do not discard' rule were broken by this PR's own additions: collectFailures' single try/catch around the whole walk converts a partial walk into a total one (a throw at depth N discards depths 0..N-1), and reportError defers process.exit to a WriteStream 'close' event whenever GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is set, so it is not a terminating function on the only platform it runs on.
validated_work_order.approach:
Three targeted repairs, each making one participant obey the rule the other two already follow. Nothing about the enumeration changes and no acceptance criterion is rewritten — all eight original criteria pass today and stay passing (verified: 91/91 green with all three prototypes applied).

BUG-1: guard the dereference in parseReleaseNotes with Array.isArray(data.authors), and on failure THROW an Error naming the note's path relative to the notes directory. Throwing rather than skipping is load-bearing: release-notes-generate.mjs:264 unlinks every entry of the `files` array, and `files` comes from listNotePaths regardless of whether the note parsed — a skipped note would be deleted unpublished, the exact 'validated, counted, then published nowhere and credited to nobody' defect this ticket exists to close, one layer down.

BUG-2: move the try/catch INSIDE the walk via an optional onError callback on listNotePaths; with no callback the walk rethrows exactly as today. collectFailures passes a callback accumulating a 'cannot read <path>: <message>' per unreadable directory and returns those alongside, not instead of, the per-note failures. The top-level directory still yields a single string (empty prefix), which keeps AC-3 true. IMPORTANT: in release-notes-gate.mjs write `path.join(dir, relative)`, not a bare `join(...)` — that file imports `* as path` and has no bare `join` binding.

BUG-3: make reportError terminating on both paths by replacing the createWriteStream(...).on('close', exit) tail with a synchronous fs.appendFileSync guarded by try/catch, followed by an unconditional process.exit(1). appendFileSync is why this works: nothing needs flushing before the process leaves. The try/catch is load-bearing — appendFileSync throws on an unwritable summary path, which would replace today's crash with a different crash at the same exit code.

The harness is what let BUG-3 hide, and this is the part the plan reviewer rejected. runCheck gains an optional second parameter for env overrides, applied AFTER `const env = { ...process.env, BASE_REF: BASE_BRANCH }`, treating an `undefined` value as a DELETE rather than stringifying it. The new BUG-3 case MUST pass `BASE_REF: undefined`; without it the case passes against the unfixed script and proves nothing.

Every new case is falsifiability-checked by reverting its source fix and recording the failure, not merely recorded green.

risks: The BUG-1 guard makes parseReleaseNotes throw a plain Error where it previously threw a TypeError. Both abort, but any future caller that caught a TypeError specifically would now catch a plain Error. No such caller exists today — release-notes-generate.mjs and generate-upcoming-release-notes.mjs both let it propagate.

The throw happens inside the files.map(async ...) in parseReleaseNotes, so Promise.all rejects and the remaining notes in that batch are never read. That is the intended abort, but one bad note stops the whole changelog rather than being skipped — the correct trade here precisely because of the unlink at release-notes-generate.mjs:264.

fs.appendFileSync in reportError is synchronous, so a large README is written on the main thread before exit. The README is a tracked file in this repository and is small; a pathological one would cost a few milliseconds, not a hang. The try/catch is load-bearing, not defensive padding: without it an unwritable summary path throws where today it produces an unhandled 'error' event, and both crash at the same exit code.

Changing collectFailures' return shape from 'either the note failures or the unreadable-directory string' to 'both' means a caller that asserted on array length or on [0] would see different output. The only caller is main(), which iterates and prints, and the unit tests, both of which are in this diff.

The chmod-000 cases are meaningless when the suite runs as root, because root ignores the permission bits. Both new permission cases must skip under root or CI running as root would record a vacuous pass.

Making runCheck's env override accept deletions is a small change to a helper thirteen existing cases share. If the merge is placed before the BASE_REF injection rather than after, the deletion has no effect and the new BUG-3 case goes vacuous again — precisely the failure the plan reviewer caught. The placement is part of the fix, not a detail.

alternatives_considered.approach: For BUG-1, SKIP the malformed note — filter it out of the map and carry on, which is what a publisher arguably wants so one bad note cannot block a release.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It silently loses data. release-notes-generate.mjs:264 unlinks every entry of the returned `files` array, and `files` comes from listNotePaths regardless of whether the note parsed — so a skipped note is deleted from upcoming-release-notes/ and never appears in any changelog. That is this ticket's original defect ('validated, counted, then published nowhere and credited to nobody') reappearing one layer down, and it would be invisible in CI because the gate never sees the file. Throwing aborts before the unlink and names the file.

alternatives_considered.approach: For BUG-1, give the publisher the gate's full validateNote and reuse it, so the two participants share one validator as they now share one walk.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: validateNote returns failure strings for a human and takes a dir plus a relative path; parseReleaseNotes needs the parsed data itself to build a changelog entry, not a verdict. Reusing the validator would mean either duplicating the parsing or reshaping validateNote into something neither caller wants. The one Array.isArray guard closes the actual crash at the actual dereference; the deeper refactor is separate work and would touch a gate this PR has already changed twice.

alternatives_considered.approach: For BUG-2, keep the single try/catch but have it return the paths accumulated so far alongside the failure string.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The walk builds its result inside a closure over `paths` and a throw discards the function's return value entirely — there is nothing to salvage without restructuring the walk anyway. Catching at the point of failure, which is what the callback does, is both smaller and the only version that keeps reporting later unreadable directories instead of stopping at the first.

alternatives_considered.approach: For BUG-3, leave reportError non-terminating and make the module-scope guard set process.exitCode and skip the rest of the file with a guard flag or an early-return wrapper.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It leaves reportError's contract as 'reports and maybe exits', which is the actual defect, and every one of its other seven call sites then has to know whether control really stopped. Making the function terminate unconditionally fixes the class rather than this call site, and appendFileSync removes the only reason the exit was ever deferred.

alternatives_considered.approach: Flip runCheck's default to SET GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, so all existing subprocess cases exercise the real Actions shape without a new parameter.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It silently redefines what six other assertions were written against, on a fix attempt, with no way to tell from the diff whether a later failure is the fix or the changed baseline. An explicit per-case override makes the environment difference visible in the test that depends on it, and leaves the thirteen existing cases untouched.

alternatives_considered.approach: Satisfy the reviewer's BUG-3 requirement without touching runCheck's env construction: have the new case delete BASE_REF by mutating process.env around the runCheck call.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would work, but it mutates the ambient environment of the whole vitest process to express one child variable, and the deletion would then be undone or not depending on which test runs next. The reviewer prescribed an explicit override parameter, it is a three-line change confined to the helper that already owns the child env, and its placement relative to the BASE_REF injection makes the deletion's mechanism legible in the diff.
